tasks.short: I build the cost and revenue view we use to look ahead.

today.trigger: FP&A opens a forecast round, or the controller asks why a site's cost moved.
steps: Export AFAS actuals by site, cost centre and ledger into Excel.
Repair links and line the totals up with last cycle's model.
Chase volume, overtime and flex hours from the three sites and the agency portals.
Read customer commitments and agency rate cards from SharePoint.
Write a short note on what the next period might cost.
drudgery: Chasing the same flex hours from three portals
today.time_sinks: Most of these hours go to assembling the sheet. The assumption that changes the number is a small slice at the end.

lenses.faster: Collecting actuals and rebuilding the Excel model is most of this work and disappears. What stays is a review of the drivers, about two fifths of the time this takes today.
lenses.autonomous: FP&A opening the forecast round, or a new volume file or agency rate card, starts a driver pack from the nightly AFAS extract. The accountant accepts the drivers before FP&A uses the number.
lenses.ambitious: Warehouse managers in Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo get a weekly cost outlook in peak season, including flex, so they can change the roster while the month is still open. Demand grows if that outlook is cheap, because flex swings between 150 and 300 people and a late quarterly pack cannot move a shift.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss copying ledger totals into Excel. The part worth keeping is the argument about which cost will actually move.
lenses.options: A base-volume case, a peak-flex case and a lost-contract case change whether the controller holds cost or accepts the spend. One combined total hides that choice.
lenses.altitude: This slice of the week becomes driver review and a conversation with the site, and the accountant gains the right to reject a driver before it enters the forecast. The job becomes more expert, because the hard part is spotting a one-off the model will otherwise extend.
reach: FP&A Analyst: the first warehouse cost bridge, after learning how each site counts volume and what they treat as a normal week.

tasks.human_edge: The accountant knows which figure is a signed contract or an agreed CAO wage step, and which is a broken dock in Venlo or a week of agency no-shows. A projection that only extends last month will miss that.
tasks.pattern_why: Volumes, rates, CAO wage steps and signed contracts can be written as a driver model and rebuilt from the ledger. An open forecast adds assumptions the workpaper cannot show back.

in_practice.trigger: FP&A opens the forecast round, or a site volume file or an agency rate card changes.
steps: Read the nightly AFAS extract by site, cost centre and ledger.
Apply the written drivers: volume, price, CAO wage steps, agency rates and known contracts.
Produce a base case, a peak-flex case and a lost-contract case, each tied to ledger totals.
Fill any variance sentence from those tables only.
Park the pack for the accountant to accept.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant accepts or edits the drivers before FP&A or a warehouse manager uses the number.
data_needed: AFAS actuals by site, cost centre and ledger
Site volume measures
CAO wage steps for both CAOs
Rate cards of the three agencies
Signed customer commitments
in_practice.logs_to: The assumption log and the pack go in the forecast folder on SharePoint, beside the FP&A model.

evidence.claim: On 160 US GAAP tasks the leading result met 61.8% of criteria, 58% were never fully solved in eight attempts, and judgement was the bottleneck. The sample is a US law firm on QuickBooks, so it does not certify a Dutch warehouse forecast.
A model that adds an unnoticed assumption leaves a workpaper that cannot be rebuilt.
Workday's Accounting Agent recommends revenue schedules from contract detail, and the team stays responsible for review.
Across 79 small and mid-sized firms, accountants using AI closed 7.5 days faster. That is a close result, not forecast accuracy, and 62% of 277 people surveyed worry about errors.

risks: A quiet wrong driver produces a forecast the sites stop trusting, which is the Finance north star.
Agency rate cards and customer commitments that live in mail or PDF will be read incompletely.
The published benchmarks are US GAAP on QuickBooks. They say judgement, not arithmetic, is where this still fails.
research_questions: What share of last year's miss on warehouse cost came from volume, flex hours and rate, and what share came from ledger noise?
Do CAO wage steps, the three agency rate cards and customer contracts already sit in AFAS or SharePoint as fields a job can read?
Will a warehouse manager change a roster on a weekly outlook, and does FP&A want this accountant to sign those drivers?
Of the 41 hours a year recorded here, how many are real outlook work and how many are one-off spreadsheet repairs?

tasks.short: I look for duplicate payments, weak controls and breaches of our rules.

today.trigger: Month close, a question from the external auditor, or a payment that looks wrong.
steps: Pull a sample of invoices, payments and user rights from AFAS.
Match the sample to the Rabobank statement.
Check a few agency invoices against hours ordered in the portals.
Look for duplicates, a changed IBAN, and the same person creating and approving.
Write up anything that still looks wrong.
today.time_sinks: The sample is small, and getting the data out takes longer than deciding whether a hit is real.

lenses.faster: Drawing samples and re-keying payments from AFAS, Rabobank and the agency portals disappears. Each hit that remains still takes a short conversation with the bookkeeper or the buyer, and a full population will raise more hits.
lenses.autonomous: The nightly AFAS extract and the Rabobank file before a batch is released start duplicate, segregation-of-duties, IBAN-change and split-invoice tests. Hits wait in a queue.
lenses.ambitious: The controller gets a match of agency hours, invoiced rate and CAO job level before each agency is paid, across all three agencies. Demand grows in peak season, when flex moves from about 150 to 300 people and the money at stake is larger.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss ticking a sample. The work worth doing is the real break: a new IBAN, a split invoice, a rate above the contract.
lenses.options: A strict match and a looser match on the same payments change which items are held and which sites are blocked by noise. That choice changes what the controller is willing to stop.
lenses.altitude: Most weeks this becomes a short exception list, and the accountant gains the right to hold a payment that fails a test. The job becomes more expert: the skill is writing the test and judging intent.
reach: Bookkeeper (accounts payable and receivable): clearing duplicate and agency-invoice matches, after learning the three rate cards and who may approve a payment in AFAS.

tasks.human_edge: The accountant has to tell a duplicate from a re-keyed receipt, a legitimate part-shipment or fraud, and a person has to speak to the buyer. The test has no view of intent.
tasks.pattern_why: Duplicates, shared approval rights, IBAN changes and split invoices are rules and can run on every posting. Calling something fraud is the judgement on the exception.

in_practice.trigger: The nightly AFAS extract lands, and again when a Rabobank payment batch is built.
steps: Test purchase invoices and payments for duplicates, split amounts under the approval limit, and IBAN changes.
Test whether the same user created and approved the invoice.
Match agency hours and rates to the three contracts where the files allow it.
Write each hit as supplier, amount, document numbers and rule, with no motive attached.
Queue the hit for the accountant.
in_practice.human_gate: A hit is a queue item. The accountant confirms it before a payment is stopped or a person is named.
data_needed: AFAS invoice, payment and approver ids
Rabobank batch and IBAN history
Agency hour files and rate cards
Approval limits in AFAS
in_practice.logs_to: The exception list sits on SharePoint for the controller. A held batch is logged there with the rule and the invoice numbers. AFAS is corrected only after the accountant confirms.

evidence.claim: Duplicate, segregation-of-duties, IBAN-change and split-invoice tests are standard audit analytics and can be coded as rules over a ledger extract.

On the accounting benchmark, judgement rather than retrieval is the bottleneck, and multi-step reasoning is over half of the leading model's errors. A rule should raise the hit; a model should not declare the fraud.
A model that adds an unnoticed assumption leaves a workpaper the auditor cannot rebuild.

risks: A noisy rule will fill the queue and two accountants will start skipping it.
Tests that name an employee or watch hours can be personnel monitoring. The works council may need to agree first, and the AVG applies to the user and payroll data.
A finding that adds a motive the records do not show will not survive the external auditor.
research_questions: How many duplicate, IBAN-change and same-user hits does one month of AFAS and Rabobank data produce, and how many are true?
Can the three agency hour files be joined to invoices on worker and week?
Who may stop a Rabobank batch today, and will the controller leave that hold with the accountant?
Will the works council treat continuous tests on user rights and hours as a monitoring system that needs agreement?

tasks.short: I compare what we budgeted with what the sites actually spent.

today.trigger: The monthly close, once site actuals are in AFAS.
steps: Take budget and actual from AFAS or from the FP&A workbook.
Rebuild a pivot by site and cost centre in Excel.
Mark the lines over budget.
Ask the bookkeeper which invoices fell in the wrong period.
Send the pack to the controller.
today.time_sinks: Formatting, and chasing invoices booked in the wrong period, uses the time. Few lines change a decision.

lenses.faster: Exporting budget and actual and rebuilding the pivot disappears. Lines over the threshold still take about a third of today's time, because the accountant checks timing with the bookkeeper and edits the sentence the controller will forward.
lenses.autonomous: The soft close, once the nightly extract holds the month's actuals, starts budget-minus-actual by site, cost centre and ledger, plus a breach list. The pack waits for approval before anyone else sees it.
lenses.ambitious: Night-shift supervisors, and the team leads in Tilburg and Venlo, get their own breach list on day 4. They are absent from the Rotterdam close meeting today. Demand grows if the list is cheap, because a lead can change the next roster only when the number arrives inside the month.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss rebuilding the pivot. The good part is the variance that is real: flex over plan, overtime, or a rate change.
lenses.options: The same month shown in full, without flex, and against a volume-adjusted budget changes whether a site looks overspent. That changes the question the controller puts to the site.
lenses.altitude: This part of the week becomes thresholds and breach conversations, and the accountant gains the right to decide which variances are large enough to escalate. The work becomes more expert about that rule.
reach: FP&A Analyst: the monthly warehouse variance commentary, after learning the volume measure that separates a real overrun from a busier week.

tasks.human_edge: The accountant can tell a timing difference, a real overrun and a budget that was wrong on day one apart. The subtraction treats all three as the same gap.
tasks.pattern_why: Budget minus actual is arithmetic on the AFAS extract, and a sentence can cite that table. A cause that is not in the table stays with the accountant, because an added assumption cannot be rebuilt.

in_practice.trigger: The nightly extract after the soft close carries a full month of actuals.
steps: Subtract budget from actual by site, cost centre and ledger.
Split flex, overtime and other warehouse cost so the views can be shown separately.
Apply the volume-adjusted budget where a site volume file is in.
List breaches over the agreed euro threshold and mark likely timing items.
Draft the breach sentence from those figures only and wait.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant approves the pack, including any sentence that names a cause, before it is published in Power BI or sent to a site.
data_needed: Approved budget by cost centre and ledger
AFAS actuals for the month
Site volumes
The controller's escalation threshold
in_practice.logs_to: The pack and the threshold log go in the close folder on SharePoint. The approved view is what Power BI shows.

evidence.claim: Where budget and actual both sit in the finance system, the comparison itself is a reconciliation, and the nightly extract is the natural source.
A model that adds an unnoticed assumption leaves a workpaper that cannot be rebuilt, so a variance sentence has to cite the tie-out.
Accountants using AI in 79 small and mid-sized firms closed 7.5 days faster. The study is not Dutch GAAP and 62% of 277 surveyed worry about errors.

risks: If the budget lives only in an FP&A spreadsheet, the nightly extract cannot produce the pack.
A volume adjustment that uses the wrong site measure will start a fight with the warehouse and weaken trust in the forecast.
A sentence carried forward from last month will hide a new breach.
research_questions: Is the approved budget in AFAS at cost centre and ledger, or only in the FP&A workbook?
What share of breaches in a normal month are invoices in the wrong period?
What euro threshold does the controller already act on?
Will a night-shift lead in Tilburg or Venlo read a Dutch breach list on day 4 and change anything?

tasks.short: I check payroll totals, premiums and wage liabilities against the ledger.

today.trigger: The Payroll Specialist closes the monthly wage run.
steps: Take the payroll totals from AFAS.
Tie gross-to-net and employer premiums to the general ledger.
Compare the loonheffingen total with the wage-tax return.
Check CAO allowances and a sample of job scales.
Flag illness cost and flex cost that look out of line.
drudgery: Matching wage codes to ledger accounts
Retyping totals that AFAS already holds
today.time_sinks: Tying a wage run that is already correct takes as long as finding the one code that is wrong.

lenses.faster: Re-footing the wage run and matching premium totals to the ledger by hand disappears. Review of the breaks stays, a wrong scale, a long-illness accrual, an agency rate off the CAO, and that review is about half of today's time.
lenses.autonomous: The Payroll Specialist closing the wage run starts a recomputation of gross-to-net, employer premiums and CAO allowances against the ledger and the loonheffingen totals. The accountant approves the figure before it enters the close.
lenses.ambitious: Flex workers paid by the three agencies enter the liability view, so Finance can see whether invoiced rates follow the hirer's CAO (inlenersbeloning) and whether a pay-parity amount is building. Demand grows with the season, because the exposure scales as flex rises from 150 to 300.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss re-adding payroll columns. The work they want is the odd case: a wrong scale, a long illness, an agency rate off the card.
lenses.options: Accruing pay during long illness at the CAO rate the company actually pays, or on a shorter expected absence, changes the liability the controller signs. Both figures belong on the page.
lenses.altitude: The month's work on this becomes the breaks and the accrual, and the accountant gains the right to keep a payroll figure out of the close when it does not tie. The job becomes more expert on wage codes and the CAOs.
reach: Payroll Specialist: the monthly tie-out of the wage return to the ledger, after learning the AFAS wage codes and the allowance tables in both CAOs. The wage run itself stays with payroll.

tasks.human_edge: A difference can be a late contract, an allowance the works council already agreed, or a real underpayment. How long a Wet verbetering poortwachter case will last is a judgement, and a tax estimate stays with the person who will stand behind the return.
tasks.pattern_why: Premiums, CAO allowance totals and the wage-return tie-out are a recomputation with a known answer. AFAS Jonas covers income tax, corporate tax and VAT and still leaves the check with the user; it does not replace this wage audit. The liability is approved every month.

in_practice.trigger: The Payroll Specialist closes the monthly wage run in AFAS.
steps: Recompute gross-to-net, employer social-insurance premiums and the loonheffingen total from the wage run.
Tie those totals to the payroll journal and the ledger.
Sum CAO allowances and scales against the allowance table.
List workers and codes that break the tie, without copying medical notes.
Hold the close entry until the accountant signs the difference and the illness accrual.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant approves the liability and any compliance exception before the number is used in the close. The Payroll Specialist still owns the filing to the Belastingdienst.
data_needed: AFAS payroll journal and wage codes
Loonheffingen return totals
CAO allowance and scale tables
Absence durations already stored in AFAS
Agency invoices and rate cards for the flex view
in_practice.logs_to: The tie-out is stored with the payroll journal in the AFAS close file and a copy is placed in the close folder on SharePoint.

evidence.claim: For this employer the generic task is the Dutch wage-tax return, employer social-insurance premiums and wage liabilities, including pay during illness. It is not a US workers' compensation audit.
AFAS Jonas assists income tax and corporate tax from 2022 and VAT from 2026, uses the return's context, and leaves the user responsible for the check. Data is not used for training.
Tax estimates belong on the mandatory human review list.

risks: Named payroll or absence data sent to an external model conflicts with the AVG. The tie-out has to stay inside AFAS, and illness detail should stay out of any draft.
An illness or premium accrual is a balance-sheet estimate and stays on the human review list.
Stopping the close over a difference the Payroll Specialist does not recognise will collide with day 3 of the close.
research_questions: By how many euros do the payroll journal, the loonheffingen return and the ledger differ in a typical month?
Which premium components are re-added by hand today, and which already tie inside AFAS?
Is absence length for open Wet verbetering poortwachter cases stored in AFAS in a form the accrual can use, without medical detail?
Is inlenersbeloning a material gap on the current agency contracts, or is it already priced into the rate cards?

tasks.short: I advise HR and Finance on the cost and tax effect of pay and systems.

today.trigger: HR or the Finance Director asks what a pay change, a benefit or an AFAS change will cost.
steps: Find the CAO article and the last memo on SharePoint.
Pull the affected cost from AFAS.
Sketch the wage-tax and corporate-tax effect from the last advisor mail.
Talk it through with Compensation and Benefits or the controller.
Rewrite the note so it can be forwarded.
drudgery: Searching SharePoint for the CAO text
Digging through old mail for the last time this was asked
today.time_sinks: Finding the last answer takes longer than giving the advice.

lenses.faster: Searching SharePoint and old mail for the CAO clause and the last memo shrinks to a check of a one-page brief. The conversation with HR, the controller and, where needed, the external tax advisor stays, and it is most of this task.
lenses.autonomous: A question from Compensation and Benefits, the HR Director or the Finance Director starts a draft brief from the CAO passage, AFAS cost and the open tax position. The accountant holds the conversation and signs anything that leaves Finance.
lenses.ambitious: The works council gets a short cost and tax note when a CAO allowance or a shift pattern is proposed, written for that agenda. Demand grows if the note is cheap, because each negotiation raises the same question and the council can ask whenever a note is easy to produce.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss hunting for last year's memo. The part they want is the session where the choice is made.
lenses.options: Paying an allowance as wage, through the werkkostenregeling vrije ruimte, or inside the agency rate changes the cost, the wage return and what the works council is likely to accept. Those three drafts are the decision.
lenses.altitude: Prep gets shorter and the meeting stays. Pay decisions stay with the HR Director and the CAO; the accountant gains a costed note those people can decide from. The job stays expert, with more of the time on the tax and CAO point.
reach: Compensation and Benefits Specialist: the first costed draft of a proposed allowance, after learning the werkkostenregeling position and the CAO text the specialist already owns.

tasks.human_edge: The accountant has to judge what the works council will accept, what a site was already promised, and what the external tax advisor will sign. A draft has no standing with the Belastingdienst or the council.
tasks.pattern_why: This is a conversation. The benchmarks that beat junior accountants left out client questions and tacit context, and tax estimates stay on the human review list. A draft brief is as far as the machine should go.

in_practice.trigger: Compensation and Benefits, the HR Director or the Finance Director asks for the cost and tax effect of a pay, benefits or AFAS change.
steps: Pull the cited CAO passage, the matching AFAS cost and the last signed memo.
Draft one page with the wage, werkkostenregeling and corporate-tax effects as alternatives.
Mark every figure that is an estimate.
Leave names and medical or absence detail out of the draft.
Hand it to the accountant, who edits it and gives the advice in person.
in_practice.human_gate: Nothing is sent to HR, the works council or the tax advisor until the accountant has signed it. The accountant gives the advice.
data_needed: Current text of both CAOs
Werkkostenregeling position and remaining vrije ruimte
AFAS cost of the population affected
Prior Finance memos and the external advisor's last written view
in_practice.logs_to: The signed memo goes in the HR-Finance folder on SharePoint. Drafts stay in the accountant's working folder.

evidence.claim: Twelve licensed accountants were beaten on month-end scenarios that reward detail and following instructions. Client communication, asking the right questions and tacit context were left out, and the study says accountants are not shown to be replaceable.
Tax estimates belong on the mandatory human review list.
In AFAS Jonas the user remains responsible for the tax-return check.

risks: A draft forwarded to HR or the works council will be read as Finance's position before the werkkostenregeling limit is checked.
The estate-planning clause in the generic task has no object in this B.V. Personal tax advice for directors is a different duty and stays out of this brief.
With two CAOs in force, a quotation from the wrong text gives the wrong cost.
research_questions: How many times a year is this accountant asked for pay, benefits or tax advice, and who decides afterwards?
Are both CAO texts, the werkkostenregeling position and prior memos on SharePoint in a form a brief can cite?
Does the works council want a Finance cost note on a proposed allowance, and does HR treat that channel as theirs?
Which piece of advice in the last year changed a decision that had not already been made?

tasks.short: I test an AFAS or interface change before we switch it on.

today.trigger: A project wants to change AFAS, the bank link, Power BI or an agency interface.
steps: Read the change note on SharePoint.
Invent a few test invoices and a payroll example.
Post them, or watch a consultant post them.
Check the journal, the VAT code and who can approve.
Say yes or no in the project meeting.
drudgery: Rewriting test cases from the last project
Sitting in the go-live week because the test started late
today.time_sinks: The accountant is often pulled in during the week of go-live, so the test is rushed and the same cases are reinvented.

lenses.faster: Rewriting the test invoices and the expected postings from scratch disappears. Walking the test in AFAS and deciding whether a defect blocks go-live still takes about three quarters of the time.
lenses.autonomous: A change request on AFAS, Rabobank, Power BI or an agency feed produces a draft test script and the postings it should create. The accountant runs the test and signs the result.
lenses.ambitious: The controller gets a go-live opinion on whether AFAS will post a real e-invoice, including intra-EU and reverse charge, ahead of the cabinet's 1 July 2030 B2B date. Demand grows as that date nears and on each AFAS upgrade, and it fades if the plan never becomes law.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss retyping the last project's script. They want the defect that would have broken the close.
lenses.options: Booking flex in the week worked, or on the agency invoice, changes the month-end cut-off. Showing both designs before go-live changes which one the accountant will sign.
lenses.altitude: A project week becomes a prepared test and a short opinion, and the accountant gains a block on go-live when the expected postings do not appear. The job becomes more expert: the call is whether a defect is a close risk.
reach: Bookkeeper (accounts payable and receivable): the acceptance checks on an invoice-posting change, after learning the AFAS approval scheme and the e-invoice fields the bookkeeper will use.

tasks.human_edge: The accountant knows the close calendar, and knows Venlo cannot repair master data on a Sunday. A script can show a wrong posting. The accountant decides whether the sites can live with a workaround for one month.
tasks.pattern_why: The checks are a known list, so the accountant can lead with a draft script. An agent walking a half-built AFAS is the multi-step failure the benchmarks already show.

in_practice.trigger: A change is proposed for AFAS, the Rabobank link, the Power BI model or an agency hour feed, before go-live.
steps: Read the change note and list the postings, VAT codes and approval rights it should produce.
Draft the test set: domestic invoice, intra-EU invoice, reverse charge, credit note, and a flex accrual if the change touches it.
The accountant posts the set in a test company and compares the journals with the script.
Record each miss with the expected and actual entry.
Write a one-page go or no-go for the controller.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant signs the test result. The change is switched on only after that signature.
data_needed: The change note and AFAS authorization design
Expected journals and VAT codes
A test company in AFAS
Sample e-invoice, intra-EU and reverse-charge documents when that change is in scope
in_practice.logs_to: The script, the actual journals and the signed go-live note go on the project's SharePoint site.

evidence.claim: The cabinet has chosen B2B e-invoicing from 1 July 2030 and reporting from 1 July 2031. It is not law yet.
A PDF is not an e-invoice. Intra-EU and reverse-charge invoices are due within 10 days in the EU design, and whether that rule applies to domestic invoices is still open.
Large companies file annual accounts with the KVK via SBR from FY2025, and AFAS cannot file that for them.
Multi-step reasoning across files is over half of the leading model's errors on accounting tasks, which is the wrong tool for exploring a half-built system.

risks: With no AFAS test company, the script stays on paper and the time saving disappears.
E-invoicing is a cabinet choice, with B2B from 1 July 2030 and reporting from 1 July 2031, and it is not law yet. A test built too early spends hours on a moving date.
If this company is in the large filing regime, AFAS cannot submit the SBR annual accounts. A go-live note that skips that point is wrong.
research_questions: How many AFAS, bank, Power BI and agency-interface changes a year reach the accountant before go-live?
Is there an AFAS test company where a domestic invoice, an intra-EU invoice, a reverse-charge invoice and a credit note can be posted?
Which defects at the last two go-lives were wrong journals, VAT codes or approval rights?
Does SBR filing of the annual accounts sit outside AFAS here, and is that in scope of the next system change?

tasks.short: I tell management what the assets and the checks showed, and what to change.

today.trigger: The controller needs the monthly story for the Finance Director and the site leads.
steps: Take the variance pack and the open audit points.
Pull utilization figures from Power BI.
Draft the note or the slides.
Agree the wording with the controller.
Explain the exceptions in the management meeting.
today.time_sinks: Making the pack look finished takes as long as choosing the one change worth recommending.

lenses.faster: Building the note from Power BI screenshots and the open-points list disappears. Editing the recommended action, and the management meeting, stay, together about three fifths of today's time.
lenses.autonomous: Once the variance pack and the control exceptions are approved, one draft writes two pages from those tables: asset use by site, open points, and one proposed change with a euro amount. The accountant approves it before it is sent.
lenses.ambitious: The operations manager at each site, including Tilburg and Venlo, gets one proposed change a month with the euro effect, in time to alter a flex order. Demand grows when the note is specific enough to use while the cost is still open, and it dies if it reads like a quarterly story for Rotterdam.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss formatting the pack. They want the recommendation a site manager actually runs.
lenses.options: From the same numbers, cutting flex hours or opening overtime for own staff changes the CAO cost and the roster. Putting both options in front of the site changes the decision a single story would hide.
lenses.altitude: Less of this week goes to the pack and more to which single change is worth the argument. The accountant gains the right to put one action on the Finance Director's list, while the site keeps the roster decision. The job becomes more expert about that choice.
reach: FP&A Analyst: the monthly management note on warehouse cost, after learning the utilization measures the sites already trust.
Controller: the first draft of the open audit-points list, after learning which points the external auditor expects in the file.

tasks.human_edge: The accountant can tell a lost customer, a seasonal peak and a real leak apart, and can tell what the CAO and the works council will accept. The largest variance is often the wrong thing to recommend.
tasks.pattern_why: The tables already exist, and one draft can turn them into a note a person checks line by line. The steps do not change from month to month. Every sentence that recommends an action is approved.

in_practice.trigger: The accountant has approved that month's variance pack and control-exception list.
steps: Read only those approved tables and the asset figures already in Power BI.
Draft two pages: utilization by site, open audit points, and one proposed change with the euro effect.
Add the flex-versus-overtime alternative where both are real.
Cite the table row under every figure.
Stop before send.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant approves every sentence that recommends an action before the Finance Director sends the note.
data_needed: Approved variance pack
Approved control exceptions
Asset and utilization figures by site
Euro effect of the proposed roster change
in_practice.logs_to: The signed note and the tables it cites go in the close folder on SharePoint. The Finance Director sends from that copy.

evidence.claim: On four month-end scenarios, twelve licensed accountants averaged about 37% and the model scored 100% on 20 attempts. The tasks reward file search and instructions. Communication, asking questions and tacit context were excluded, and the authors say accountants are not shown to be replaceable.
Across 160 US GAAP tasks, 58% are never fully solved in eight attempts. Judgement is the bottleneck.
A model that adds an unnoticed assumption produces a workpaper that cannot be rebuilt.
A shipped finance agent that recommends a revenue schedule still leaves the team responsible for review.

risks: A fluent note that adds a cause the tables do not show will be forwarded and can move a roster for the wrong reason.
Dock, trailer and forklift utilization may sit in operations sheets outside the nightly AFAS extract, so the asset section would be invented.
A note written for the Finance Director will not be read by a site manager who needed a roster decision.
research_questions: Did the operations managers in Tilburg or Venlo act on any finance recommendation in the last four quarters?
Are dock hours, pallets or cost per order in the nightly extract, or in a separate operations file?
Which recommended actions from the last year were carried out, and which were only discussed?
Will the Finance Director keep the accountant's approval on every action sentence before the note goes out?

role.altitude: The week moves from rebuilding samples, pivots and wage tie-outs to keeping the driver rules, the control tests and the close checks that run before the meeting. The accountant gains the right to reject a forecast driver, hold a payment that fails a test, keep an untied payroll figure out of the close, and place one action on the Finance Director's list. The job becomes more expert: the scarce work is a CAO point, a tax position, a real control break and a conversation with a site.
reach: Bookkeeper (accounts payable and receivable): duplicate and agency-invoice matches, after learning the three rate cards and the AFAS approval paths.
FP&A Analyst: the warehouse cost bridge, the variance commentary and the first management note, after learning how each site measures volume and utilization.
Payroll Specialist: the monthly tie-out of the wage return to the ledger, after learning AFAS wage codes and both CAO allowance tables. The wage run stays with payroll.
Controller: the first draft of the audit-points log and the go-live test note, after learning what the external auditor expects in the file.
role.ceiling_note: Two accountants cannot absorb FP&A, payroll and the controllership. These seven tasks are about 14% of the role; the month close, the statutory file and the VAT and corporate tax positions sit beside them and stay reviewed by a person. The benchmarks that beat junior accountants are US GAAP exercises and do not cover Dutch GAAP, Dutch VAT or an audit file. Full-population tests add a queue of exceptions, and peak season can lift flex from 150 to 300. The works council and the AVG limit checks on named employees. The Belastingdienst, the external auditor and the OR still deal with a person.
skills_to_grow: Writing tie-outs and control tests on AFAS data that an auditor can rebuild: duplicates, segregation of duties, IBAN changes, wage-return differences.
Driver-based warehouse forecasting from site volumes, CAO wage steps and the three agency rate cards.
Loonheffingen, employer premiums, the werkkostenregeling and both CAOs, well enough to see a wrong accrual.
Pre-go-live test design for AFAS, including e-invoices, intra-EU and reverse charge, and where SBR filing sits.
What the works council must be asked before a check monitors named employees.
role.ambitious_version: Every journal, payment, wage total and agency invoice is tested before the close meeting. The accountant's month is the forecast drivers the three sites will argue with, the few control breaks that are real, and a short costed note a site manager or the works council can act on. Days to close and audit adjustments move because the tie-outs already exist. Forecast accuracy, shared with FP&A, is the measure of whether the advice was any good.
